Svíčka: čtyři ceny v jednom obrázku: The candle: four prices in one picture
Každá svíčka ukazuje, kde cena za dané o: Each candle shows where price opened for the given period (open), how high and low it went (high, low) and where it closed (close). The body is the distance between open and close, the wicks are where price went and came back from. A long wick says: the market tried here and was rejected.
Svíčka má čtyři ceny: open, high, low a: A candle has four prices: open, high, low and close. The body is between open and close, the wicks show where price went and came back from.
Dlouhý horní knot znamená, že cena šla n: A long upper wick means price went up but could not hold there.
Knot je místo, kam cena zašla a byla odm: A wick is a place where price went and was rejected.
Co říká dlouhý horní knot svíčky?: What does a long upper wick tell you?
Cena tam zašla a byla odmítnuta: Price went there and was rejected
Trh byl v tu dobu zavřený: The market was closed at that time
Knot ukazuje, kam cena došla a odkud se: A wick shows where price got to and where it returned from. The body ends at the close.
Co řekl dlouhý dolní knot: What a long lower wick said
Svíčka zajela pod dvě stejná dna a zavře: The candle dipped below two equal lows and closed back above them. A long wick remained.
Knot ukazuje odmítnutí nižších cen. Kupu: The wick shows a rejection of lower prices. I buy only after the candle closes and put the stop below the wick.
Když další svíčka zavře pod knotem, odmí: When the next candle closes below the wick, the rejection is invalid.

Začíná se nahoře (den, hodina) a postupn: You start at the top (day, hour) and gradually zoom in.

Směr beru z hodinového grafu. Na pětimin: I take the direction from the hourly chart. On the five-minute I wait for the end of the correction and buy.
Když korekce prorazí poslední dno hodino: When the correction breaks the last low of the hourly chart, the trend is no longer valid.

Obchod hledám jen v živé části dne. V kl: I look for a trade only in the lively part of the day. In quiet hours I don't take the same picture.
Když je den bez pohybu i po otevření, ne: When the day has no movement even after the open, I leave it alone.

Svíčka má dlouhý horní knot a malé tělo: A candle has a long upper wick and a small body at the bottom. What happened during it?
Cena vyšla vysoko, ale kupci ji tam neud: Price went up high, but buyers couldn't hold it there and sellers pushed it back almost to the opening price. The market was rejected up there.
Struktura trhu I: swingy a trend: Market structure I: swings and trend
Poznáš na grafu trend nahoru, trend dolů: You recognise an uptrend, a downtrend and sideways movement on the chart.
Swing high je svíčka, která má vyšší hig: A swing high is a candle with a higher high than the candles to its left and right. A swing low is the same reversed with the low. They are the points where the market turned. Everything else in market structure is built from these points.
Swing high má vyšší high než sousední sv: A swing high has a higher high than the neighbouring candles, a swing low a lower low. They are the points where the market turned.
Swing low je svíčka, která má nižší low: A swing low is a candle with a lower low than the candles to its left and right.
Exactly, it is the mirror of the swing high.
Nejvyšší cena celého dne: The highest price of the whole day
Svíčka s vyšším high než svíčky vlevo i: A candle with a higher high than the candles to its left and right
Swing high je místní vrchol: sousední sv: A swing high is a local top: the neighbouring candles have lower highs.
Stop patří za swing: The stop belongs behind the swing
The market made a swing low and is rising from it.
Kupuju nad swingem a stop dávám těsně po: I buy above the swing and put the stop just below it. The swing is the place where price turned.
Když cena swing low prorazí, moje čtení: When price breaks the swing low, my reading was wrong and the stop takes me out.
Trend nahoru znamená, že každý nový vrch: An uptrend means each new high is higher than the previous one (higher high) and each new low is higher too (higher low). A downtrend is the mirror: lower highs and lower lows. As long as this sequence holds, the trend lasts.
Trend nahoru znamená vyšší vrcholy a vyš: An uptrend means higher highs and higher lows. A downtrend means lower highs and lower lows.
V trendu nahoru je každé nové dno níž ne: In an uptrend each new low is lower than the previous one.
V trendu nahoru jsou dna čím dál výš (hi: In an uptrend the lows keep getting higher (higher low).
Jak vypadá trend nahoru?: What does an uptrend look like?
Rostoucí trend dělá higher high i higher: A rising trend makes a higher high and a higher low.
Vyšší vrcholy a vyšší dna. Cena se vrací: Higher highs and higher lows. Price returns to the last higher low.
Kupuju v návratu, stop pod poslední vyšš: I buy on the pullback, stop below the last higher low, target above the last high.
Když padne poslední vyšší dno, trend nah: When the last higher low falls, the uptrend has ended.
Když cena nedělá ani vyšší vrcholy, ani: When price makes neither higher highs nor lower lows, it moves in a band between an upper and lower boundary. The market spends most of its time like this. For a beginner it is the hardest environment, so learn mainly to recognise it and leave it alone.
Range je pohyb do strany mezi dvěma hran: A range is sideways movement between two boundaries. Learn to recognise it and leave it alone.
Range je pro začátečníka nejlehčí prostř: A range is the easiest environment for a beginner to trade.
Je nejtěžší, proto je lepší ho jen pozna: It is the hardest, so it is better to just recognise it and not trade.
Trh je v range. Co má začátečník udělat?: The market is in a range. What should a beginner do?
Vstupovat uprostřed pásma: Enter in the middle of the band
Poznat ho a nechat být: Recognise it and leave it alone
Range je nejtěžší prostředí. Stačí ho ro: A range is the hardest environment. It is enough to recognise it and wait.
Range: obchod, který nevezmu: Range: a trade I won't take
Cena se čtyřikrát odrazila mezi dvěma hr: Price bounced four times between two edges. No higher highs or lower lows.
Nedělám nic. Uprostřed pásma není výhoda: I do nothing. There is no edge in the middle of the band and the edges often break falsely.
Začnu se zajímat, až cena z pásma jasně: I start to pay attention once price clearly leaves the band and holds outside.
Trend neběží rovně. Střídá se v něm siln: A trend doesn't run straight. A strong move in the trend's direction (impulse) alternates with a slower return against it (correction). Traders don't want to jump in at the end of an impulse; they wait for the correction and enter at a better price.
Trend střídá impuls a korekci. Vstupuje: A trend alternates impulse and correction. You enter in the correction, not at the end of the impulse.
Nejlepší cena pro vstup bývá na konci si: The best entry price tends to be at the end of a strong impulse.
You wait for the correction, where the price is better.
Kdy se v trendu vstupuje za lepší cenu?: When do you enter at a better price in a trend?
Na konci impulsu: At the end of the impulse
V korekci je cena výhodnější a stop může: In the correction the price is better and the stop can be closer.
Vstup v korekci, ne na vrcholu: Entry in the correction, not at the top
Rychlý impuls nahoru a po něm pomalá kor: A fast impulse up followed by a slow correction in small candles.
Nekupuju na konci impulsu. Čekám na kore: I don't buy at the end of the impulse. I wait for the correction, where the price is better and the stop closer.
Když je návrat stejně rychlý jako impuls: When the return is as fast as the impulse, it is not a correction and I don't enter.
Na hodinovém grafu NQ si za poslední dva: On the hourly NQ chart mark all swing highs and swing lows over the last two weeks. For each stretch write whether it is an uptrend, a downtrend or a range.
Trh udělal vyšší vrchol, ale následné dn: The market made a higher high, but the next low is lower than the previous one. Is it still an uptrend?
Už ne jistě. Řada vyšších den se přeruši: Not for certain any more. The series of higher lows was broken, so the trend is at least weakened and may be changing. That is next week.
Struktura trhu II: zlom a změna směru: Market structure II: break and change of direction
Rozlišíš pokračování trendu od jeho obra: You tell a trend continuation from its reversal and can read structure on multiple timeframes.
Break of structure (BOS) je průraz posle: A break of structure (BOS) is a break of the last swing in the trend's direction. In an uptrend price closes above the last high. It is confirmation that the trend is alive. A candle body close beyond the level counts, a wick alone is not enough.
BOS je zavření těla svíčky za posledním: A BOS is a candle body close beyond the last swing in the trend's direction. The trend continues.
K BOS stačí, když úroveň prorazí jen kno: For a BOS it is enough when only a candle's wick breaks the level.
Počítá se zavření těla za úrovní, knot n: A body close beyond the level counts, a wick is not enough.
Knot svíčky krátce přesáhne poslední swi: A candle's wick briefly exceeds the last swing
Tělo svíčky zavře za posledním swingem v: A candle body closes beyond the last swing in the trend's direction
Cena se posledního swingu jen dotkne: Price only touches the last swing
Počítá se zavření těla za úrovní. Samotn: A body close beyond the level counts. A wick alone is not enough.
Po BOS čekám na návrat: After a BOS I wait for a return
Svíčka zavřela tělem nad posledním swing: A candle closed with its body above the last swing high. The uptrend is confirmed.
Nekupuju průraz. Čekám, až se cena vrátí: I don't buy the breakout. I wait for price to return to the broken level and buy there.
Když cena zavře zpátky hluboko pod úrovn: When price closes back deep below the level, the BOS failed.
Market structure shift (MSS, někdy CHoCH: A market structure shift (MSS, sometimes CHoCH) is the first break against the trend. In an uptrend price closes below the last higher low. It doesn't mean a certain reversal, it means the first warning that strength is shifting.
MSS je první zavření proti trendu. Je to: An MSS is the first close against the trend. It is a warning, not a certain reversal.
An MSS means the trend has certainly turned.
Je to jen první varování, že se síly pře: It is only a first warning that strength is shifting.
Co znamená MSS v trendu nahoru?: What does an MSS mean in an uptrend?
První varování, že se síly přesouvají: A first warning that strength is shifting
MSS je první zavření proti trendu. Je to: An MSS is the first close against the trend. It is a warning, not a certainty.
MSS jako první varování: The MSS as a first warning
Trh rostl, vybral vrchol a pak zavřel po: The market rose, took a high and then closed below the last higher low.
Po MSS čekám na návrat nahoru a prodávám: After the MSS I wait for a return up and sell. I put the stop above the high.
Když cena udělá nový vrchol, MSS byl fal: When price makes a new high, the MSS was false.
Zlom, který proběhne rychle a velkými sv: A break that happens fast with large candles has more weight than a slow crawl through the level. That fast move is called displacement and you will meet it in week five. For now just notice what the break looks like.
Rychlý zlom velkými svíčkami má větší vá: A fast break with large candles has more weight than a slow crawl through the level.
Zlom velkými rychlými svíčkami je silněj: A break with large fast candles is a stronger signal than a slow crawl through the level.
Tomu rychlému pohybu se říká displacemen: That fast move is called displacement.
Který zlom úrovně má větší váhu?: Which break of a level has more weight?
Rychlý, velkými svíčkami: A fast one, with large candles
Pomalé prolezení malými svíčkami: A slow crawl with small candles
Rychlý zlom ukazuje skutečný zájem. Říká: A fast break shows real interest. It is called displacement.
Silný zlom beru, slabý ne: I take a strong break, not a weak one
Úroveň prorazily velké svíčky s plnými t: Large candles with full bodies broke the level and price kept going.
Silnému zlomu věřím víc. Vstupuju při ná: I trust a strong break more. I enter on the return to the level.
Kdyby se cena přes úroveň jen přeplazila: If price had only crawled over the level with small candles, I would skip the trade.
Hodinový graf může být v trendu nahoru,: The hourly chart can be in an uptrend while the five-minute is falling right now. It is not a contradiction; the five-minute drop is just a correction of the hourly trend. The higher timeframe sets the direction, the lower is for timing.
Směr určuje vyšší timeframe. Pohyb proti: The higher timeframe sets the direction. A move against it on a lower chart is just a correction.
Když hodinový graf roste a pětiminutový: When the hourly chart rises and the five-minute falls, it is a contradiction and nothing can be read from it.
Pětiminutový pokles je jen korekce hodin: The five-minute drop is just a correction of the hourly trend.
Hodinový graf roste, pětiminutový zrovna: The hourly chart is rising, the five-minute is falling right now. What is it most likely?
Konec hodinového trendu: The end of the hourly trend
Korekce hodinového trendu: A correction of the hourly trend
Směr určuje vyšší timeframe. Pohyb proti: The higher timeframe sets the direction. A move against it on a lower chart is just a correction.
Korekce malého grafu ve velkém trendu: A small-chart correction in a big trend
Hodinový graf roste. Pětiminutový klesá,: The hourly chart is rising. The five-minute is falling, but holds above the hourly low.
Čekám, až pětiminutový graf otočí nahoru: I wait for the five-minute chart to turn up and buy in the direction of the hourly.
Když padne hodinové dno, nejde o korekci: When the hourly low falls, it is not a correction and I cancel the trade.
Najdi na 15minutovém grafu deset míst, k: Find ten places on the 15-minute chart where a BOS happened and five places where an MSS happened. For each MSS look whether the trend really changed direction afterwards, and write down the result.
Jaký je rozdíl mezi BOS a MSS?: What is the difference between a BOS and an MSS?
BOS je průraz ve směru stávajícího trend: A BOS is a break in the direction of the existing trend and confirms it. An MSS is the first break against the trend and warns of a possible change of direction.
Víš, kde na grafu leží stop-lossy ostatn: You know where other people's stop-losses lie on the chart and why price goes to them.
Kdo je v longu, má stop-loss pod nějakým: Whoever is long has a stop-loss below some low. Whoever is short has it above a high. That is why pending orders build up in these places. ICT calls them liquidity: above highs it is buy-side, below lows sell-side.
Likvidita jsou nahromaděné stop-lossy. N: Liquidity is accumulated stop-losses. Above highs it is buy-side, below lows sell-side.
Pode dny leží stop-lossy těch, kdo jsou: The stop-losses of those who are long lie below lows.
Uprostřed range: In the middle of a range
Nad vrcholy mají stop-lossy ti, kdo jsou: Those who are short have their stop-losses above highs. Their stops are buy orders.
Dvě stejná dna vedle sebe. Pod nimi leží: Two equal lows side by side. Buyers' stop-losses lie below them.
Nekupuju na dně. Čekám, až cena stopy vy: I don't buy at the low. I wait for price to take the stops and return above the level.
Když cena pod dny zůstane, byl to průraz: When price stays below the lows, it was a breakout and not a liquidity grab.
Nejčitelnější úrovně jsou high a low pře: The easiest levels to read are the previous day's high and low, the overnight session's high and low and places where the market has two or more highs or lows at almost the same price (equal highs, equal lows). The more visible a level is, the more stops lie at it.
Nejvíc stopů leží u viditelných úrovní:: The most stops lie at visible levels: yesterday's high and low, the overnight session's and equal highs or lows.
Čím je úroveň na grafu viditelnější, tím: The more visible a level is on the chart, the fewer stops lie at it.
Je to naopak, viditelná úroveň přitahuje: It is the opposite; a visible level attracts more stops.
U které úrovně čekáš nejvíc stop-lossů?: At which level do you expect the most stop-losses?
U náhodné ceny uprostřed dne: At a random price in the middle of the day
U ceny, kde se nikdy nic nestalo: At a price where nothing ever happened
Čím je úroveň viditelnější, tím víc stop: The more visible a level is, the more stops lie at it.
Cena se blíží k viditelnému vrcholu, nad: Price is approaching a visible high above which sellers' stops lie.
Čekám, jestli cena vrchol jen propíchne: I wait to see whether price only pokes through the high and comes back. Then I sell with the stop above the wick.
Když cena nad vrcholem zavře a drží se,: When price closes above the high and holds, I don't take the short.
Sweep je krátké proražení úrovně, po kte: A sweep is a brief break of a level after which price quickly comes back. The stops were taken and the market turned. A real breakout, on the other hand, stays beyond the level and continues. You can tell the difference only by what price does afterwards, never in advance.
A sweep briefly breaks the level and comes back. A real breakout stays beyond it. You know only afterwards.
Jestli jde o sweep, nebo o průraz, se dá: Whether it is a sweep or a breakout can be told in advance.
Pozná se to až podle toho, co cena udělá: It can be told only by what price does after the break.
Jak rozlišíš sweep od skutečného průrazu: How do you tell a sweep from a real breakout?
Podle barvy svíčky: By the colour of the candle
Poznáš to předem podle času: You know in advance from the time
Až podle toho, co cena udělá potom: Only by what price does afterwards
Sweep se rychle vrátí zpět, průraz za úr: A sweep quickly comes back, a breakout stays beyond the level. You don't know in advance.
Sweep poznám až podle návratu: I recognise a sweep only by the return
Svíčka zajela pod úroveň a zavřela zpátk: A candle dipped below the level and closed back above it.
Vstupuju až po návratu, ne při propíchnu: I enter only after the return, not on the poke. Stop below the wick.
Kdyby svíčka zavřela pod úrovní a další: If the candle had closed below the level and the next one continued, it would be a breakout.
ICT se u každého grafu ptá: ke které lik: For every chart ICT asks: which liquidity will price most likely go to next? He calls this target level the draw on liquidity. It serves as both the direction and the trade target.
Draw on liquidity je úroveň, ke které ce: The draw on liquidity is the level price is most likely heading for. It gives the direction and the target.
Draw on liquidity slouží jako směr i jak: The draw on liquidity serves as both the direction and the trade target.
That is why ICT asks about it for every chart.
K čemu slouží draw on liquidity?: What is the draw on liquidity for?
Jako místo pro stop-loss: As a place for the stop-loss
Jako směr i cíl obchodu: As the direction and target of the trade
Je to úroveň, ke které cena nejspíš míří: It is the level price is most likely heading for. It gives the direction and the target.
Cíl je další likvidita: The target is the next liquidity
Trend nahoru a nad cenou starý vrchol, k: An uptrend and above price an old high where stops lie.
Směr i cíl mi dává ten vrchol. Kupuju v: That high gives me both the direction and the target. I buy in the correction and take profit just below it.
Když cena začne dělat nižší dna, k vrcho: When price starts making lower lows, it is no longer heading for the high.
Každý den po dobu jednoho týdne si před: Every day for one week, before 15:30 mark the previous day's and the overnight session's high and low on the NQ chart. In the evening look at which levels price took and what it did next: a sweep or a breakout?
Cena vyskočí nad včerejší high, během dv: Price jumps above yesterday's high, within two minutes returns below it and falls. What is it called and what happened to the short sellers' stops?
Je to sweep buy-side likvidity. Stop-los: It is a sweep of buy-side liquidity. The short sellers' stop-losses above the high triggered as buys and it was possible to sell big against them.
Displacement a fair value gap: Displacement and the fair value gap
Poznáš silný pohyb a mezeru, kterou po s: You recognise a strong move and the gap it leaves behind.
Displacement je rychlý, jednosměrný pohy: Displacement is a fast, one-directional move with large candles and small wicks. It shows that one side completely took over the market for a moment. In ICT it is proof that there is real interest behind the move, not just noise.
Displacement je rychlý pohyb jedním směr: Displacement is a fast move in one direction with large candles and small wicks.
Displacement poznáš podle malých svíček: You recognise displacement by small candles with long wicks.
It is large candles with small wicks.
Velké svíčky jedním směrem s malými knot: Large candles in one direction with small wicks
Displacement je rychlý jednosměrný pohyb: Displacement is a fast one-directional move where one side took over the market.
Displacement ukazuje, kdo má navrch: Displacement shows who has the upper hand
